transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-05
- Time: 15:00 PST
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Jessica Park (Redwood AE), Tom Reynolds (Redwood SE), Sara Nguyen (EnterpriseFinance CTO), Martin Lopez (Head of Security), Aisha Khan (Identity Engineer)

Summary: quick kickoff, then deep dive on SAML & SCIM provisioning, RBAC mapping, and encryption options; several clarification questions on retention and BYOK; clear next steps and owners.

[00:00] Jessica Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i have Tom from our security and identity team with me, we'll run through how our SSO and SCIM integration works and then talk RBAC patterns for least privilege.
[00:18] Sara Nguyen: Great thanks, quick FYI we are evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for latency and data residency reasons, security is the gating factor for us so wanted to make sure RBAC and key management line up.
[00:30] Martin Lopez: Yes specifically we need audit logs with tamper evidence and a way to retain for 2 years, also BYOK or HSM support is important - we can't have keys managed entirely by the vendor for some data.
[00:45] Tom Reynolds: Totally makes sense. On SSO we support SAML 2.0, most customers use Okta or Ping, we can map SAML assertions to Redwood roles and groups. For SCIM we support SCIM 2.0 provisioning for users and groups, group-to-role mapping is done server-side.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: When you say map groups to roles, can we map multiple IdP groups to a single Redwood role? And is that mapping configurable from your console or through an API?
[01:12] Tom Reynolds: Yes you can map multiple groups to a role. We expose that mapping in the console under Identity -> Mappings and also via the Admin API so infra automation is possible. There is a caveat: if you want attribute-based role assignment (like dept=trading -> limited-access role) we support claim mapping from SAML attributes, not just group names.
[01:35] Sara Nguyen: Ok is that claim mapping documented? Our IdP has custom attributes we need to pass through.
[01:40] Tom Reynolds: We'll share the SCIM + SAML claim mapping guide after the call — it has example assertions and sample Okta configs. We'll also include a sample SAML metadata xml and a test SP entry.
[02:05] Martin Lopez: SCIM provisioning - how often do you sync groups? We're concerned about stale groups lingering and over-privileged accounts.
[02:13] Tom Reynolds: SCIM is event-driven for most IdPs upsert events, but we also run a nightly reconciliation job. For customers that need near-real-time we support push notifications from Okta/Ping and we can lower reconciliation window; frequency is configurable.
[02:35] Aisha Khan: Does SCIM support custom group attributes and nested groups? We have nested team groups.
[02:41] Tom Reynolds: We have partial support for nested groups — in the SCIM mapping you can flatten or preserve nesting depending on how you want to map to Redwood roles. Custom group attributes can be ingested as meta attributes and used in attribute-based access decisions, though some customers prefer to do the mapping in the IdP and keep Redwood mappings simple.
[03:05] Sara Nguyen: Alright about audit logs: can you export raw logs to our SIEM? We use Splunk and want immutable logging for admin actions.
[03:12] Tom Reynolds: Yes audit logs are available via an API stream and we support delivery to S3 buckets or to syslog endpoints; many customers push to Splunk. Logs include user, action, timestamp, IP, and request IDs. For tamper evidence we provide append-only write patterns and signed log manifests for enterprise plans.
[03:40] Martin Lopez: What about retention controls? Need 24 months by default for certain roles.
[03:45] Jessica Park: On our Enterprise plan we can set retention windows and export to customer-managed S3 for long-term archival; we can also set retention policy to comply with your data retention schedule.
[03:58] Aisha Khan: Encryption — specifically BYOK. We need to bring our own key on an HSM that we control, or at minimum a KMS in our cloud account. How does Redwood handle that?
[04:10] Tom Reynolds: We support BYOK in two flavors: customer-managed KMS in cloud (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) where Redwood uses a grant pattern to encrypt at rest, and a dedicated HSM option for on-prem/private deployments. For hosted customers we do offer a managed KMS but for enterprise we can do BYOK with key rotation policies you control.
[04:35] Martin Lopez: Is there an option for envelope encryption with your runtime so that model cache or KV cache doesn't keep plaintext?
[04:42] Tom Reynolds: Yes we do envelope encryption — server-side keys wrap per-tenant data keys, the wrapped keys are stored encrypted with your KMS. Our runtime does not keep unencrypted long-term caches, and in Dedicated/Private deployment paths you can opt to keep the KV cache within your VPC or on disks encrypted with your keys.
[05:05] Sara Nguyen: Any limitations on feature parity if we go Dedicated or Private? For example do we lose streaming, or tool-calling?
[05:12] Jessica Park: Feature parity is maintained for API features. The difference is operational: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and private networking; Private can be air-gapped and provides more control over keys and logs. We can share feature matrix in the follow-up.
[05:30] Martin Lopez: For SAML role mapping: how do you prevent privilege escalation if someone is added to a group in IdP accidentally? Any approval flows?
[05:38] Tom Reynolds: We recommend using short-lived role assignments, SCIM deprovisioning and automatic revocation, plus we support admin approval flows via the console for sensitive roles — e.g., require manual approval for roles tagged as "high-privilege". Additionally, we give visibility in the audit logs for any change events with pre-change and post-change snapshots.
[06:05] Aisha Khan: How are service accounts handled? We need machine-to-machine identities for jobs that call Redwood APIs. Do they have separate RBAC and non-expiring keys?
[06:13] Tom Reynolds: Service accounts are first-class: they map to a Principal with token lifetimes you can configure, short lived by default with rotation via our API. For long-running jobs we recommend rotating tokens monthly and using our scoped tokens with least privilege. We also support certificate-based auth for service accounts in Private deployments.
[06:45] Sara Nguyen: Any common gotchas from previous customers doing SCIM+SAML?
[06:50] Tom Reynolds: A few: claim name mismatches (email vs userPrincipalName), groups with different naming schemes, and provisioning race conditions when both IdP and manual changes happen. We provide a pre-check script and an import dry-run mode to catch mapping issues before going live.
[07:10] Martin Lopez: SOC2 and compliance artifacts — can we get your Type II report and the list of controls?
[07:15] Jessica Park: Yes, we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO documentation under an NDA; we also have a compliance pack with our control matrix.
[07:25] Aisha Khan: About SAML attributes — can you accept full NameID format and persistent identifiers? We need stable IDs for account linking.
[07:31] Tom Reynolds: Yes NameID persistent is supported; we recommend using a stable immutable identifier to avoid duplicates.
[07:45] Sara Nguyen: For groups-to-roles mapping, can we test mapping in a staging project before syncing to production?
[07:51] Tom Reynolds: Absolutely—we provide staging tenants and a dry-run for SCIM syncs. We'll set up a test SP and give you credentials for the staging environment.
[08:05] Martin Lopez: For the RBAC model itself, any recommended role sets for finance orgs? We want least privilege but reasonably granular.
[08:13] Tom Reynolds: A typical pattern: 1) Read-only role for analysts, 2) Limited-edit for dev/tools, 3) Admin with audit-only actions, 4) Sensitive-admin with approve flows. We usually keep roles coarse and then use attribute-based checks for specific resource-level controls.
[08:40] Aisha Khan: How is deprovisioning handled if an employee leaves — immediate token revocation?
[08:45] Tom Reynolds: SCIM deprovisioning triggers immediate account disable and we revoke active sessions and tokens. There's a short window for long-lived refresh tokens but we can enforce immediate revocation for sensitive roles.
[09:00] Sara Nguyen: Anything about data residency? We need all logs and stored data in US regions.
[09:05] Jessica Park: We support region pinning for storage and compute — on Dedicated we can pin to US-only regions and on Private you control the region entirely. We'll capture your required regions in the SOW.
[09:20] Martin Lopez: One more on KMS: key rotation — can we force rotation every 30 days and have Redwood accept rotated keys without downtime?
[09:28] Tom Reynolds: Yes, our KMS integration supports key rotation and a rolling re-wrap process so there is no downtime. For HSMs we have a rotation protocol and can schedule key rollover windows.
[09:45] Jessica Park: Ok i'll quickly recap next steps — we'll send SOC2 and encryption whitepaper, Tom will share SCIM/SAML mapping guide and sample metadata, we'll schedule an RBAC mapping workshop week of 12/14, and Jessica will send pricing for Dedicated + BYOK. Aisha will share the list of SAML attributes.
[10:05] Sara Nguyen: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:10] Martin Lopez: Appreciate it, thanks.

End of transcript.
